DILG ; Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triang:e, Quezon City http://www.dilgx;om.ph SO JUL 2019 OILG OPINION No. s. 204 HON. CELSO OLIVER T. DATOR Municipal Mayor Lucban, Quezon Deaf Mayor Dator: This pertains to your letter dated 28 January 2019 Lo Dir. Darrell I. Dizon, Provincial Director, DILG Quezon Province regarding the approval of annual budget, specifically on the voting requirement to enact an appropriation ordinance. Relative thereto, please be informed that this Department had already settled the issue on the required votes for passing an appropriation ordinance. DILG Legal Opinion No. 13 S. 20101 discussed thoroughly the same, and uve quote: "For purposes ofc/arity, please allow us to discuss the terms quorum, "simple majority, " and "qualified majority. " For the sanggunian to officially transact business; there should be a quorum. A quorum is defined by Section 53 of the Local Government Code of 1991 as referring to the presence of the majority of a/j the members of the sanggunian who have been duly elected and qualifieü. Relative thereto, generally, 0Fdinary measures require for its enactment only the approval of a simple majority of the sanggunian members present, there being a quorum. These pertain to the normal transactions of the sanggunian which are approved by the sanggunian through a vote of simple majority of those present. On the other hand, there are certain measures where the Local Government Code requires for its approval the vote cn rnajority of all the memberS who were duly elected and qualified. This is vvnat we call approval by the qualified majority of the sanggunian. In this case; the approval is to be voted not just by the majority of those present in a session there being a quorum but by a majority of all the members of the sanj'cunian duly elected and qualified regardless of whether all of them were p;esent or not in a particular session, there being a quorum. Having these definitions in mind, may we now invite your attention to the following provisions of the Local Government of 1991, viz: 09 February 2010 page 1 of 3

"SECTION 139. Legislative Authorization of the Budget. — On or before the end of the current fiscal year, the sanggunian concerned shall enact, through an ordinance, the annual budget of the local government unit for the ensuing fiscal year on the basis of the estimates of income and expenditures submitted by the local chief executive. " "Section 468. Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. (a) The sangguniang panlalawigan, as the legislative body of the province, shall enact ordinances, approve resolutions and appropriate funds for the general welfare of the province and its inhabitant pursuant to Section 16 of this Code and in the proper exercise of the corporate powers of the province as provided for under Section 22 of this Code, and shall: xxx (2) Generate and maximize the use of resources and revenues for the development plans, program objectives and priorities of the province as provided for under Section 18 of this Code, with particular attention to agro-industrial development and country-wide growth and progress and relative thereto, shall: (i) Enact the annual and supplemental appropriations of the provincial government and appropriate funds for specific programs, projects, services and activities of the province, or for other purposes not contrary to law, in order to promote the general welfare of the province and its inhabitants;" Based on the foregoing, on or before the encl of the current fiscal year, the sanggunian concerned (the Sangguniang Pan;aåvigan in yoru case) shall enact, . through an ordinance, the annual budget of the Province of Cotabato for the ensuing fiscal year on the basis of the estimated of income and expenditures submitted by Governor Sacdalan. The legislative instrument authorizing the budget is known as an Appropriation Ordinance. •Please note that Section 468 (2) (i) of the Local Government Code Of 1991, providing for the powers of the Sangguniang Pan/u!awigan vests unto said sanggånian the power to appropriate the annca/ and supplemental appropriations of the provincial government, and appropriate funds for specific programs, projects, services and activities of the province, and for other purposes not contrary to law. It is to be noted thar with respect to the enactment of the annual and supplemental appropriations, the law is silent as to what kind of majority vote is required of that sanggunian, unlike succeeding provision which specifically require qualifieå :najority vote of that sanggunian for their passage. In its silence, the presumption is, the same is to be enacted only by a simple majority vote. Page 2 Of 3

As to the argument that the Appropriation is an o; dinance authorizing or directing the payment of money so that it requires the vote of a majority of all the Sangguniang Pan/alawigan Members for its passage, Section 55 of the Local Government Code of 1991 would bolster the position that the Appropriation Ordinance and an Ordinance directing the payment of money or creating liability are different when said provision treated them separately. Section 55 (b) of the same Code provides that: "The local chief executive, except the punong barangay, shall have the power to veto any particular item or items of an appropriation ordinance, an ordinance or resolution adopting a local development plan and public investment program, or an ordinance directing the payment of money or creating liability xxx". As already mentioned, the Appropriation Ordinance is the legislative instrument authorizing the annual budget. Hence, what is there to be authorized by the sanggunian is the Annual Budget. An Annual Budget does not provide for the direction to pay or create a liability but it refers to a financial plan embodying the estimates of income and expenditures for one (I) fiscal year operations ofa local government unit. We are of the opinion that what is being referred co under Article 107, 2nd sentence of paragraph (g) of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of the Local Government Code of 1991 which requires the approval ofa qualified majority vote is an ordinance or resolution (specific appropriations) authorizing or directing the payment of money or creating a liability. " In view of the above-cited DILG Opinion,' this Department is of the position that the required vote to pass an appropriation ordinance is oniy simple majority. Nonetheless, upon scrutiny of your letter, it appears that the attached document re: Kapasiyahan B/g. 002-1018 which disapproved the annual budget for 2019 of your Municipality is in order as the required number ot votes to pass the said appropriation ordinance was not obtained (4 affirmative votes and 5 negative votes). We hope we had addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Copy furnished: DIR. MANUEL Q. GOTIS, CESO 111 Regional Director DILG Region IV-A Brgy. Parian, Calamba, Laguna LIIs/37 Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: MARIVEL C. S CENDONCILLO, CESO 111 Undersecretary page 3 Of 3
